Data Appreciation · Week 6 · Title

Spreadsheets II: formulas that do the work

Formulas calculate for you, and recalculate when the data changes: SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, COUNT — and fill down.

Next Generation Genius · Year 1 · Foundation

Data Appreciation · Week 6 · Goals

By the end of today

  • Write formulas with SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX and COUNT
  • Fill a formula across or down
  • Explain relative and absolute references
Data Appreciation · Week 6 · Idea 1

Understand it

A formula starts with =. A function is a named calculation; a range is the cells it works on.

  • =SUM(B2:B5) adds B2 to B5.
  • =AVERAGE(B2:B5) · =MIN(…) · =MAX(…) · =COUNT(…) counts numbers.
  • =B2*C2 multiplies two cells; + - * / all work.

Change a number and every formula that uses it updates. That is the whole point: never type a total you could calculate.

Fill: drag the small square at the corner of a cell. The references move with it — =SUM(B2:B5) becomes =SUM(C2:C5) one column right. That is a relative reference.

Data Appreciation · Week 6 · Idea 2

Understand it

Sometimes one cell must NOT move — a tax rate in E1. Write it $E$1: an absolute reference. =B2*$E$1 filled down always uses E1.

If you ask an AI chatbot to write a formula, test it on numbers you can check by hand before you trust it — it is often confidently wrong about ranges.

Data Appreciation · Week 6 · Key words

Key words

Formula
a calculation that starts with =
Function
a named calculation such as SUM
Range
a block of cells, like B2:B5
Absolute reference
a reference with $ that does not move when filled
Data Appreciation · Week 6 · Practice

Now you do it

  2. Fill it across three days
  3. Work out a 7.5% charge using an absolute reference

Data Appreciation · Week 6 · Assessment

How you will be assessed

  • Write a formula to find the average of the values in D2 to D10.
  • C6 holds =SUM(C2:C5). You fill it one column right into D6. What does D6 hold?
  • Complete the GCFGlobal Google Sheets lesson on formulas and functions and its practice; paste proof and one formula you wrote yourself.

Your work is marked against the rubric, and you may be asked to explain your choices. Show your own thinking.
